abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, yet they are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of pentabenzocorannulenide (PBC−), a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide (Cp−) ring. The five-membered Cp− ring is generated quantitatively by aromatization-driven nucleophilic dealkylation (C–C bond cleavage) of a pentabenzocorannulene derivative. Through single crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum chemical analyses, we reveal the unique structural features and physicochemical properties of PBC−, demonstrating uncommon bonding pattern and electronic characteristics distinct from corannulene, fullerenes, end caps of carbon nanotubes and other geodesic polyarenes. PBC− has an exceptionally strong conjugate acid, undergoes reversible covalent functionalization and engages in η5-type metal complexation. Incorporating the iconic Cp− ring into a fully conjugated sp2 carbon network opens avenues for exploring non-conventional π systems.

title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core
source: Nature
abstract: Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are two types of biogenetically related polycyclic monoterpenoid alkaloids with distinct structural features. Reported synthetic strategies typically construct the core architectures of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids independently, and no protocol enabling their simultaneous synthesis has yet been developed. Herein, we describe the assembly of both eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloid skeletons from a common alkoxyallene precursor, a characteristic that aligns with their inherent biogenetic connection. Our investigations reveal that upon Prins-type spirocyclization of the alkoxyallene under Brønsted or Lewis acid catalysis, the intermediate undergoes two discrete tandem reaction pathways: Mannich-like cyclization/migration to construct the skeleton of eburnane alkaloids under Brønsted acid catalysis, whereas nucleophilic addition to the indole iminium assembles the aspidofractinine alkaloids framework under Lewis acid catalysis. The developed divergent cascade cyclization strategy has been successfully applied to the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids including (−)-eburnamonine, (−)-eburnamenine, (+)-eburnamine, and (±)-aspidofractinine.

title: Exciton-phonon interaction suppression enables efficient near-infrared perovskite quantum dot LEDs
source: Matter
abstract: In energy-transfer light emitters, lattice vibrations can drain energy before recombination and reduce near-infrared emission efficiency. This study uses an ion-pair treatment to change the surface of Yb-doped perovskite quantum dots, which reduces vibration-related losses and improves energy transfer. The resulting devices produce efficient, bright near-infrared light under electrical operation. The findings suggest that controlling lattice dynamics through surface chemistry can improve this dual-channel emitter.

title: Mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology for high-performance integrated circuits
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Low-dimensional semiconductors, such as one-dimensional carbon nanotubes and two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides, could be used to build scaled, energy-efficient electronic devices. However, although these materials can exhibit excellent unipolar device performance, complementary integration with balanced performance and low power consumption remains a challenge. Here we report a mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology that combines two-dimensional single-crystal molybdenum disulfide n-type transistors and one-dimensional aligned carbon nanotube p-type transistors. We integrate enhancement-mode top-gate transistors with symmetric threshold voltages using a hard mask technology and pre-deposition annealing process. We use the approach to create complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor inverters that exhibit rail-to-rail operation with a peak static power of less than 1 pW and a single-stage delay of 19 ps. We also fabricate 180-nm-node area-equivalent static random-access memory that offers robust read–write operations with a noise margin of 22% and 40% operating voltage. The uniformity of the transistors and inverters also allows us to create basic logic gates and a 4-bit full adder.

title: Antifreeze proteins in action: structural determinants, hydration dynamics, and ice-binding mechanisms

abstract: Anchored by classical nucleation theory, this review connects the structural diversity of antifreeze and ice-nucleating proteins to their ice-binding mechanisms and extends to cryopreservation, anti-icing, and AI-driven mimetic design.

title: Field‐Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two‐Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4‐fluorophenylethylammonium (4‐FPEA), is shown to brighten dark excitons in (4‐FPEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    without an external magnetic field. Below 30 K, (4‐FPEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    exhibits a sharp photoluminescence (PL) signal 7.8 meV below the bright exciton that is absent in (PEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4
                    . Its long lifetime, strong linear polarization, and quadratic magnetic‐field dependence identify this signal as dark‐exciton emission. A magnetic field of up to 0.7 T changes this emission only weakly, whereas it strongly brightens dark excitons in (PEA)
                    2
                    PbI
                    4

                    2

Under two‐photon excitation, which generates excitons deep inside the crystal, the dark‐exciton emission persists. The brightening, therefore, originates in the bulk, unlike the surface‐related brightening reported for other 2D R–P perovskites. These results identify spacer fluorination as a simple chemical route to access spin‐forbidden excitonic states in 2D R–P perovskites.

title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. Ru incorporation induces structural disorder and enhances Fe─O covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen participation in seawater oxidation. Meanwhile, oxophilic silver oxide reconstructed in situ establishes an OH
                    −
                    ‐enriched interfacial environment that mitigates Cl
                    −
                    adsorption and rapidly replenishes LOM‐generated oxygen vacancies, thereby stabilizing the catalyst structure. Consequently, Ag‐RuFeCo LDH requires only 308 mV overpotential to achieve 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    in alkaline natural seawater and maintains stable performance during a cumulative operation exceeding 9500 h. An anion‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzer using Ag‐RuFeCo LDH as both electrodes reaches 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    at 1.92 V and operates continuously for 1000 h with a low energy consumption of 4.59 kWh Nm
                    −3
                    H
                    2
                    . This strategy successfully overcomes the corrosion bottleneck of LOM in seawater electrolysis and offers a general strategy for durable and sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Thermodynamically Controlled Multiphase Evolution in Single‐Crystal Cation‐Disordered Li‐Ion Cathode Materials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Mn‐based disordered rock‐salt (Mn‐DRX) cathodes are promising materials for Li‐ion batteries, yet their application is limited by sluggish Li transport, voltage instability, and capacity fading. Here, we show that thermodynamic control of multiphase evolution from single‐crystal Mn‐DRX overcomes these limitations. Using grand‐potential phase diagrams with in situ and ex situ X‐ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, we demonstrate that DRX composition and annealing conditions govern transformation into nanocomposites containing DRX, spinel, and monoclinic layered phases, with anatase formation predicted in specific Li–Mn–Ti–O compositions. Oxidative annealing at 300–500°C induces decomposition pathways: Li‐deficient compositions form DRX–spinel (DS) nanocomposites, whereas Li‐rich compositions form DRX–spinel–monoclinic layered (DSM) architectures. Unlike DS materials, which exhibit lower first‐charge capacities than discharge capacities, the monoclinic phase in DSM nanocomposites enables substantially improved first‐charge Li extraction, critical for practical Li‐ion batteries. The DSM nanocomposites deliver reversible capacities approaching 300 mAh g
                    −1
                    and discharge specific energies exceeding 800 Wh kg
                    −1
                    , while their cycling stability can be substantially improved by using a highly concentrated electrolyte and restricting the voltage window. This work establishes thermodynamically guided multiphase engineering as a strategy for addressing transport and stability limitations in DRX cathodes.

title: Multiscale Characterizations Toward Energy Storage Carbon Materials From Precursors to Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The sp
                    2
                    ‐hybridized carbon materials such as graphite, soft carbon, and hard carbon, are broadly used as anodes for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries owing to their stable and controllable microstructures. However, the inherent structural complexity and multi‐stage synthesis processes of carbon materials pose challenges to their comprehensive characterization, limiting a deeper structural understanding and performance improvement of carbon electrodes. This review establishes a comprehensive characterization framework for the multiscale understanding of carbon materials from their precursors to carbon electrodes. Because the structural features of carbon materials are largely inherited from their precursors, we first summarize the recent advances in the characterization of their molecular structures and pyrolysis behaviors. We then discuss advanced characterization techniques and corresponding analysis methods used to understand the multiscale structures of carbon materials, including particles, microcrystals, and pore structures. We further provide a comprehensive overview of static and real time characterization techniques for studying interfacial ion transport and bulk ion diffusion kinetics in carbon electrodes. On this basis, we draw a decision‐making framework for multiscale characterization to help readers quickly navigate from problem definition to characterization strategy. Finally, we provide future perspectives to facilitate the efficient scientific investigation and rational design of high‐performance carbon materials for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries.

title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the
                    C9orf72
                    gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR
                    20
                    ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR
                    20
                    . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR
                    20
                    is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR
                    20
                    -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR
                    50,
                    we found PR
                    50
                    synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR
                    50
                    or GR
                    50
                    expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.

title: Music illuminates sociocultural dimensions of autobiographical memory
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Researchers have long theorized that autobiographical memory relies on sociocultural structures, such as life scripts and event schemas. The potency of music as a marker of social and personal identity, combined with its ubiquity in everyday life, allows us to connect these everyday scripts to larger patterns of socially and culturally shaped behavior. We collected free-response descriptions of autobiographical memories evoked by short clips of familiar songs from university undergraduates (n = 233). The songs spanned three popular genres and aligned with two significant periods of listeners’ lives. We analyzed the similarities and differences in the content of memories for particular songs using natural language processing. Memories cued by songs from the same category displayed striking similarities, suggesting that particular types of music cue memories that are similar between listeners but that vary according to characteristics such as music genre and release date. Two control conditions, in which a new set of participants reported memories evoked by key words from the lyrics (n = 121) and short narrative summaries of the lyrics (n = 129), indicate that these results cannot be explained by within-category similarities in the songs’ lyrical content. Instead, we suggest that the intersubjective structure of music-evoked autobiographical memories reflects socioculturally-defined scripts tied to song characteristics such as genre and release date. Thus, while memories may feel idiosyncratic and personal, there are also substantial similarities in life experiences between individuals with broadly similar backgrounds, and these shared experiences can be spontaneously called to mind through the seemingly innocuous act of turning on the radio.

title: Coupled human–cattle mobility shaped the socioeconomic landscapes of the Holocene Middle Nile Valley
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a synthesis of strontium isotope data (
                    87
                    Sr/
                    86
                    Sr) from human and cattle dental enamel across Middle Nile. This dataset, which combines newly acquired and published measurements, reveals a complex history of human and cattle mobility linked to ecological gradients and sociocultural changes in this part of the continent. During the early Holocene (8,000 to 4,000 BCE), isotopic unanimity in human and cattle remains supports early, correlated mobility of humans and
                    Bos
                    , extending beyond Nile floodplains to adjacent uplands. In the mid-Holocene (4,000 to 1,000 BCE), isotopic data from Wadi Howar suggest bidirectional corridors for mobility of both species linking the Middle Nile and the Western Desert. This pattern correlates with the emergence of the Middle Nile civilizations in which cattle played a central cultural and economic role. From the first millennium BCE onward, a radical change can be observed, correlated with the progressive desertification processes in the Sahel. Although cattle import routes continued to follow wadi systems, they shifted south of the now desiccated Saharan lakes toward Kordofan. The long-term perspective emphasizes the continuous adaptation of societies in the Middle Nile of what is now Sudan and adjacent regions to environmental changes, aimed at maintaining sustained access to cattle, a resource that remained crucial for Middle Nile communities throughout the Holocene.

title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and robotic devices.

title: Impact pathways of a jurisdictional approach to slowing deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Governance of many of the world’s largest remaining tropical forests is shared across multiple levels of government, giving subnational jurisdictions a central role in forest management. This has motivated growing interest in jurisdictional approaches (JAs) to control deforestation. For JAs to deliver on national and international conservation priorities, those priorities must be translated into incentives that reduce deforestation at the jurisdictional level. Brazil’s Priority List (PL), launched in 2008, creates such incentives by identifying high-deforestation municipalities, subjecting them to intensified monitoring, enforcement, and credit restrictions, and establishing jurisdiction-wide criteria for exit that make municipalities accountable for deforestation within their borders. While prior studies show that the PL reduces deforestation, it remains unclear where these reductions occur and whether there is displacement across land tenure types or into neighboring municipalities. We assemble a municipality-level panel dataset for the Brazilian Legal Amazon (2000–2024) that combines PL designations with annual deforestation disaggregated by land tenure. Using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimator, we estimate effects within and across municipalities. We find large and statistically significant reductions concentrated on private lands, including agrarian reform settlements and other private properties. Within listed municipalities, we find no evidence of decreased or increased clearing in Protected Areas, Indigenous Territories, or undesignated public lands. Total deforestation also declines in neighboring municipalities, with reductions concentrated on private lands. These findings are consistent with the PL translating national conservation priorities into local land-use change while limiting displacement, offering insights for the design of jurisdictional approaches aimed at forest conservation.

title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.

title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI
                    c
                    1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI
                    c
                    1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

title: A decadal record of isotopic trends in martian atmospheric CO2
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
This work represents the first long-term record of the isotopic composition of martian atmospheric CO
                    2

                    2
                    isotopes. Coordinated pairs of analyses during MY 31 and 38 revealed no significant differences in isotopic composition of CO
                    2
                    acquired during daytime and nighttime hours. However, here we show evidence for modest enrichment in heavy isotopes of oxygen in both northern and southern hemisphere spring-summer seasons. We assessed several processes, including precipitation/sublimation and adsorption/desorption of CO
                    2
                    , CO
                    2
                    photolysis, and oxygen isotope exchange as potential candidates for producing the observed fractionations. We find that while sublimation of CO
                    2
                    from polar caps, sublimation and desorption of CO
                    2
                    from lower latitude reservoirs, and CO
                    2
                    photolysis are insufficient alone, we can reproduce the measured enrichment through modeling of isotope exchange between CO
                    2
                    and
                    18
                    O-enriched H
                    2
                    O in thin liquid-like films at Mars’ surface or adsorbed within the regolith as Mars approaches and transits through perihelion. Lesser
                    18
                    O enrichment near aphelion may reflect less favorable conditions for oxygen isotope exchange at lower temperatures. Observed seasonal variations in CO

Since our measurements were obtained at a single near-equatorial location on Mars, the relative contributions from global, regional, and local processes cannot be well-constrained by the available data.

title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA)
                    Gaplinc
                    is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish
                    Gaplinc
                    as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While
                    Gaplinc
                    knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic
                    Gaplinc
                    overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that
                    Gaplinc
                    functions
                    in trans
                    and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary
                    Gaplinc
                    binding partner. Loss of
                    Gaplinc
                    drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that
                    Gaplinc
                    bridges transcriptomic immune regulation with systemic lipid and metabolic output, dictating survival outcomes in systemic inflammation.

title: isSPA-vesicle: AI-assisted structure determination of membrane proteins on vesicles
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The demand for three-dimensional reconstruction of membrane proteins in native lipid environments has grown substantially in recent years. Both single-particle analysis and tomographic techniques have enabled structural studies across diverse vesicular samples; however, these methods remain limited in either efficiency or resolution. Here, we present an AI-enabled, vesicle geometry-guided 3D reconstruction strategy based on untilted data. Given that some vesicles exhibit anisotropic shapes in solution and adopt near-spherical or ellipsoidal geometries, we trained an AI model to estimate membrane geometric parameters and compute normal vectors based on the fitted ellipsoidal surface. This information facilitates post hoc filtering of particles picked using the isSPA framework based on the angular difference between their orientations and the membrane normals, and also enables the exclusion of particles outside the vesicles. This allows efficient localization of target membrane proteins enabling near-atomic-resolution reconstruction. Using this approach, we efficiently reconstructed membrane proteins ranging from 130 kDa to 2 MDa across two classes of enveloped viruses and three types of synthetic liposomes, achieving 2.7 Å resolution for influenza A virus hemagglutinin and 3.1 Å for the prefusion spike protein of HCoV-OC43. Our method provides a simple and efficient tool for achieving such reconstructions in physiological lipid bilayers.

title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature (
                    P-T
                    ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock
                    P-T
                    state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme
                    P-T
                    conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.

title: Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia: A 10-y follow-up
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Vacant lot greening has been shown to reduce violence and crime in the short-term [C. C. Branas
                    et al.
                    ,
                    Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A.
                    115
                    , 2946–2951 (2018)]. We assessed the 10-y impact of a 2013 clustered randomized controlled trial (RCT) of lot greening in Philadelphia on violence and crime. We measured lot greening by treatment assignment from the original 2013 cluster RCT and a longitudinal greening score to assess the sustainability of the treatment assignment from 2012 through 2023. Our outcomes were the annual reported total crime, violent crime, and firearm violent crime per square mile at each lot. We conducted intent-to-treat and contamination-adjusted intent-to-treat analyses to estimate the local average treatment effect on relative change in crime. Lots randomized to the full greening intervention remained greener over time compared to other lots. In intent-to-treat analyses, compared to lots that received no intervention, lots that received any intervention had a 9% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.96) and a 9% decrease in violent crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.97) per square mile per year. In contamination-adjusted analyses, compared to lots without sustained greening treatment, lots with sustained greening treatment had a 12% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.93) and an 11% decrease in density of violent crime (estimate = 0.89, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.95) per square mile per year. Even after a decade, vacant lot greening continues to prevent violence.

title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health. Reconstructing this indicator allows insights into which types of societies were providing better health and nutrition—also termed the “biological standard of living” in the literature. Yet, archaeological evidence has not previously been assembled on a scale large enough for systematic comparison across premodern Eurasia. We present a dataset of 18,457 stature observations based on 783 sites from Asia and Europe, roughly spanning the 7,000 y before the twentieth century. Using harmonized estimates derived from long bones, we document broad regional variation in stature over time and examine how these patterns relate to population density and historical indicators of technological development. We observe marked declines in stature in most regions during the 500–1900 CE period, in both Asia and Europe. To interpret these patterns, we combine our stature series with estimates of population density, technological advancement, and related controls. As [Q. Ashraf, O. Galor,
                    Am. Econ. Rev.
                    101
                    , 2003–2041 (2011)] predicted, higher technology levels were associated with higher population density, but not correlated with higher stature before the modern era. This relationship also holds after controlling for other potentially confounding factors such as latitude or transport access. By assembling the largest archaeological stature dataset for Eurasia to date and linking it to long-term demographic and historical indicators, this study provides an empirical basis for comparative research on premodern health, nutrition, and population pressure.

title: Distinct nanoscale architectures of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predict diverse synaptic output
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
GABAergic synaptic inhibition is heterogenous across neuronal compartments, and plays a critical role in shaping local, cellular, and circuit excitability. In pyramidal neurons, inhibition is mediated by GABA
                    A
                    receptors (GABA
                    A
                    Rs) clustered at the inhibitory postsynaptic domain (iPSD). Synaptic strength depends not only on the number of GABA
                    A
                    Rs within the iPSD, but also on their precise nanoscale organization into discrete subsynaptic domains (SSDs). These SSDs often align with presynaptic GABA release sites to form nanocolumn structures that enhance synaptic efficacy. While nanocolumn organization is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of synaptic function, most studies of GABAergic synapses have focused on archetypal dendritic synapses, which control the plasticity and integration of excitatory inputs. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether somatic synapses—which deliver robust inhibition to suppress neuronal output—share a similar nanoarchitecture. Here, we used complementary superresolution imaging approaches to directly compare inhibitory synapses in somatic and dendritic compartments. We found that somatic synapses are larger and exhibit greater structural diversity and nanoscale complexity than dendritic synapses. Dendritic synapses display relatively compact architectures with GABA
                    A
                    R SSDs frequently arranged into nanocolumns. In contrast, somatic synapses show a broader range of organizations, including aligned nanocolumns as well as more disorganized configurations with misaligned release sites or receptor SSDs, arrangements that likely exhibit input-specificity. Computational modeling revealed that these structural differences produce distinct functional outcomes, including increased inhibitory postsynaptic current amplitude and altered kinetics at somatic synapses. Together, our findings demonstrate that nanoscale organization differentially shapes inhibitory strength and signaling properties across neuronal compartments.

title: China’s energy transition strategy favoring both coal and renewables: Economic risks and global implications
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: China’s energy strategy is navigating a complex policy landscape: While leading the world in renewable energy manufacturing and deployment, it is simultaneously pursuing a continued expansion of its coal-fired power fleet. This paper examines this dual trajectory by building an integrated analytical framework that combines domestic and international perspectives to analyze the social, economic, climate, and geopolitical impacts of China’s new coal-power plant investments. Combining historical trends, government planning, and projections from influential policy teams, we find that a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030, a pace China is on track to meet, is sufficient to satisfy all projected electricity demand scenarios when considered alongside the evolving generation mix and planned storage deployment. We further show that additional coal capacity is not required to ensure adequate electricity supply under these scenarios. The coal pathway could expose up to $223.6 billion of stranded assets from new projects and add an additional 327,000 workers in a declining industry. Furthermore, this trajectory may weaken the alignment between China’s domestic energy investment and its international clean energy leadership. We conclude that a clean-energy-led pathway that halts new coal construction is lower-cost, better for job growth, and more consistent with China’s role as a leader in the global clean energy transition.

title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. With a median of 11 high-noise vessel exposures per day, these disruptions may result in an average daily shortfall of 4.6% of their net energy budget. Sustained over time, such noise-induced energetic deficits have the potential to compromise individual fitness, ultimately affecting the dynamics of harbor porpoise populations in industrialized coastal areas worldwide and reducing their functional carrying capacity. This framework establishes a direct mechanistic link between behavioral disruption and fitness-relevant impacts, providing a biologically grounded metric for predicting population-level outcomes of noise pollution and an objective basis for defining acceptable exposure levels of vessel noise for wild marine mammal populations. Moreover, it is scalable across species and ecosystems and offers a common currency for assessing the cumulative effects of multiple stressors in the Anthropocene oceans. As vessel traffic and its associated noise outputs continue to increase globally, our results offer timely insights for evidence-based management, and support efforts to balance the societal demand for low-cost maritime transport with the responsibility to ensure the sustainable use and conservation of marine biodiversity.

title: Direct CO2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO
                    2
                    into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO
                    2
                    activation typically requires coreactants, high temperatures, or significant electrical input, any of which increases cost or limits scalability. Here we demonstrate a straightforward way to split CO
                    2
                    directly into carbon monoxide and oxygen using light. By combining a light-driven antenna-reactor photocatalyst with a material that acts as an oxygen reservoir, CO
                    2
                    can be decomposed directly into CO and oxygen with light only. Under illumination, photoexcited carriers induce CO
                    2
                    bond dissociation, while cerium oxide adsorbs the released oxygen into vacancy sites, preventing recombination. The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO
                    2
                    conversion, shifting the chemical equilibrium of CO
                    2
                    dissociation in a controllable manner.

title: Leptin Receptor+ cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR
                    +
                    ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR
                    +
                    cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14.
                    Cxcl14
                    -expressing LepR
                    +
                    cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of
                    Cxcl14
                    from LepR
                    +
                    cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from
                    
                      Lepr-cre; Cxcl14
                      fl/fl
                    
                    mice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in
                    
                      Lepr-cre; Cxcl14
                      fl/fl
                    
                    mice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to promote platelet formation by megakaryocytes in vitro and in vivo. LepR
                    +
                    cells thus create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis by producing CXCL14, which regulates lipid metabolism and terminal differentiation in megakaryocytes.

title: The evolution and function of eukaryote-to-cyanobacteria horizontal gene transfer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Prokaryote-to-eukaryote horizontal gene transfer (HGT) has emerged as a driver of eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, eukaryote-to-prokaryote HGT remains poorly characterized, limiting insight into how eukaryote-derived genes influence prokaryotic evolution and function. Here, we reconstructed a comprehensive and well-resolved phylogeny of 469 high-quality Cyanobacteria genomes spanning all orders. Leveraging this framework, we identified 204 candidate functionally diverse genes of eukaryotic origin in cyanobacteria, likely representing 59 putative transfer events, including 197 genes not previously documented. All 204 candidates were intronless, consistent with intron loss during their evolutionary history. Transcriptomics reveal that HGT-acquired genes are expressed at significantly higher levels than both genome-wide and functionally matched non-HGT-acquired genes, suggesting functional importance. Notably, 138 genes exhibited functional annotations absent from the host cyanobacteria. We further characterized a granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS) putatively acquired by
                    Crocosphaera
                    from an ancestral archaeplastid lineage, enabling starch synthesis that may facilitate energy storage for nocturnal nitrogen fixation. These findings reveal that eukaryote-to-prokaryote gene transfer is an underappreciated driver of cyanobacterial evolution and function, with broad implications for microbial ecology, functional adaptation, and cross-domain genetic exchange.

title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper’s primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of “peak water” and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps, environmental flow protections, and enhanced monitoring networks.

title: Transoceanic dispersals and island extinctions shape global snipe and woodcock diversity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Island colonization through transoceanic dispersal has been central in shaping insular biodiversity. Following colonization, island populations often undergo morphological shifts, which may promote ecological specialization and endemism, but often increase vulnerability to extinction. Most species in the shorebird family Scolopacidae are highly migratory, which likely underpins their propensity for long-distance dispersal. Notably, snipes (
                    Gallinago
                    ,
                    Coenocorypha
                    ) and woodcocks (
                    Scolopax
                    ) have colonized diverse island regions, including the southwest Pacific, Malay Archipelago, Japan’s Amami, and the Caribbean, although none of the extant island endemics are migratory. The southwest Pacific and Caribbean taxa have suffered substantial recent extinction driven by human impacts. Here, we investigate avian evolutionary and biogeographic dynamics using a combination of morphology and phylogenomic data from target capture sequencing of key extant and extinct snipes and woodcocks. Our results reveal four independent dispersals from the Eastern to Western Hemisphere and a trans-Pacific dispersal from South America to the southwest Pacific islands. Comparative analyses of migratory behavior and morphology demonstrate pronounced changes in insular groups. For example, the small Austral snipes
                    Coenocorypha
                    are nested within
                    Gallinago
                    , sister to a group of much larger, continental South American snipes. Another case is the extinct
                    Scolopax brachycarpa
                    of Hispaniola which osteologically more resembles
                    Scolopax
                    , but genetically belongs to
                    Gallinago
                    .
                    Gallinago brachycarpa
                    and other extinct Caribbean snipes may represent a radiation that is lost forever. Our findings shed light on the processes that generate and erase avian diversity on islands, highlighting the dynamic interplay of dispersal, adaptation to novel conditions, and risk for extinction.

title: Short-term flexibility and long-term stability in models of mind perception
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Understanding how people decide whether someone or something possesses a mind is central to a myriad of psychological, biological, and philosophical questions. It shapes fundamental processes at the individual (e.g., social interaction) and societal level (e.g., morality and ethics). While mind perception has been studied, it remains unclear which internal model people use when ascribing mental capacities to entities. Across four experiments (total N = 256), we explored what model people hold and its flexibility when ascribing agency and experience to entities encountered in everyday life and which differ in animacy and socialness (e.g., humans, pets, robots, voice assistants, tools). Using representational similarity analysis combined with lab-based experiments, a 6-wk long social interaction intervention, and longitudinal real-life exposure, we tested which model people use to ascribe agency and experience by comparing observed rating data to theoretical models. We demonstrated that an animacy distinction underlies the representational structure of experience attributions, while internal models for agency attributions are more idiosyncratic and flexible. When receiving explicit information on one entity, the internal model of agency changes. People update their model by incorporating this information, generalizing across the entire category of entities. We found no evidence that extended exposure to or ownership of inanimate technology, such as robots or voice assistants, or pets leads to restructuring of the models for experience or agency. Overall, these results provide insight into the internal models people hold when perceiving minds, the flexibility thereof, and offer ways to understand the roots and consequences of mind perception.

title: No evidence for a universal effect of writing on language use or the evolution of syntax
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The acquisition of writing has a lasting effect on how languages are processed in the brain, raising the possibility that it also affects how they are used and evolve over time. A popular hypothesis is that writing specifically leads to the increased use and evolution of complex hierarchical structures in language. While most case studies on individual languages have supported this, it remains unclear whether results scale to larger and more diverse sets of languages. Here we test this prediction in two ways: 1) synchronically, by modeling the effect of modality (written vs. nonwritten) on syntactic complexity, operationalized via hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences, in corpora from 30 languages; and 2) diachronically, by modeling whether the development of writing affected the phylogenetic dynamics of hierarchy in clause combinations across 59 languages from three families. We found no effect of writing on the response variables in either analysis. Hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences do not demonstrably differ between spoken and written use of language, and the introduction of writing had no discernible effect on the evolution of clause combinations in grammar. There is weak evidence for a decrease in variance in structural asymmetry after the introduction of writing in one family, possibly reflecting the impact of increased normativity. Our findings challenge popular beliefs about the relationship between writing and hierarchy and suggest that the evolution of syntax is more driven by culturally variable ideas about style in linguistic expression than by the evolution of writing.

title: Calculated residue protonation states find functional, conserved E-channel proton-loading sites in Complex I from bacteria to mammals
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Bioenergetic proton pumps take protons from one side of a membrane, transiently binding them at a loading site within the protein matrix, and then release them to the other side against an electrochemical gradient. The E channel of Complex I, from bacteria to mammals, contains a conserved proton-loading region whose function is distributed among several interacting residues. Noting extensive sequence divergence across homologous Complex I structures, we asked how this function is conserved during evolution despite many amino acid changes. Multi-Conformation Continuum Electrostatics (MCCE) calculations were performed on the five E-channel subunits from 41 experimental structures from bacteria, cyanobacteria, insects, and mammals. A Monte Carlo sampling identified five to seven residues in each species that function as a proton-loading cluster. Structures with a closed E-channel have ~1 more proton in the cluster than those with open conformations. Proton binding represents ensemble averages across thousands of accessible microstates, each with an integer protonation state. A mean-field analysis showed that the proton affinity depends on both titrating residues and the surrounding protein electrostatic environment. Closely related proteins use nearly the same cluster of residues, whereas more divergent proteins substitute alternative proton-handling residues and modify electrostatically important fixed-charge groups to preserve cluster proton affinity. Thus, E-channel reversible proton-loading is preserved during sequence evolution by maintaining a local “electrostatic architecture,” often involving quite different evolutionary solutions. Thus, conservation of E-channel proton loading depends more strongly on the local electrostatic environment than on conservation of the individual residues that create it.

title: A Neandertal-derived genetic variant reduces occipital brain volume in present-day humans
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Neandertal crania were less globular than those of modern humans, suggesting differences in the relative volumes of brain regions, including the frontal and occipital lobes. Here, we show that a common genetic variant influencing occipital brain volume in present-day people was inherited from Neandertals. The variant lies in predicted transcription-factor recognition motifs near
                    DAAM1
                    , a gene that is known to be involved in brain development. Carriers of the Neandertal variant have altered
                    DAAM1
                    expression and occipital lobe volumes that are about 0.85 cm³ smaller per gene copy. The variant is associated with reduced schizophrenia risk by almost 10% in homozygous carriers, while Neandertal ancestry as a whole does not show such a tendency. Any association with cognition or schooling is small or nonexistent, amounting to at most two weeks of education per allele against an average of about 15 y. Thus, this Neandertal-derived variant is linked to altered brain anatomy in present-day humans and lower schizophrenia risk while having little or no association with general cognitive ability.

title: An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The interrupted Pummerer reaction is a time‐honored and enduringly versatile tool in organic synthesis, and has recently found widespread application in the preparation of aryl sulfonium salts. However, the classical interrupted Pummerer protocol suffers from long‐standing intrinsic limitations: (a) The key reactants, sulfoxides, are rarely commercially available; (b) the use of harsh electrophilic activator often leads to limited functional‐group tolerance. To address these issues, we have herein developed a Selectfluor‐mediated oxidative interrupted Pummerer variant, which is applicable to synthetic C─H functionalization, allowing approaches to a range of aryl sulfonium salts, including thianthrenium, dibenzothiophenium, and phenoxathiinium frameworks. The present strategy circumvents the use of electrophilic activator and directly utilizes sulfides as starting materials, thereby enabling the scope to be expanded to unprotected amine‐containing arenes.

title: Iron‐Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Achieving precise site‐selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron‐catalyzed protocol for accessing C3‐amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ‐generated Fe–acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach was also successfully implemented in a telescoped one‐pot procedure by directly employing pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies revealed that a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical would be the key amidating species.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO2 Catalyst
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H
                    2
                    ) and methane (CH
                    4
                    ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO
                    2
                    ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO
                    2
                    nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO
                    2
                    catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO
                    2
                    catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H
                    2
                    and CH
                    4
                    . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the electrooxidation of 2‐butanol (SBA) offers an energy‐efficient route to co‐production of hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), yet achieving selective MEK formation while maintaining sustained operation remains challenging because of sluggish anodic kinetics and product accumulation. Here, we integrate alloy‐catalyst engineering with reaction–rectification to address these coupled catalytic and process‐level limitations. A self‐supported PdAu/NF anode exploits Pd–Au ligand interactions to regulate the adsorption of SBA, surface hydroxyl species and MEK, thereby suppressing C─C bond cleavage and facilitating product desorption. The optimized PdAu/NF catalyst delivers 300 mA cm
                    −
                    2
                    at 0.74 V versus RHE. Despite weakened MEK adsorption, accumulated MEK and MEK‐derived intermediates inhibit SBA oxidation on PdAu and hydrogen evolution on Pt. At the process level, membrane‐free PdAu/NF||Pt/NF electrode arrays are integrated with reaction–rectification, enabling continuous MEK removal, recovery and SBA recycling. This in situ product separation mitigates product accumulation and its inhibitory effects, enabling continuous electrolysis at 14 A with a cell voltage of approximately 1.3 V over 10 h. The integrated system produces MEK with 99% purity while simultaneously generating hydrogen, highlighting the potential of coupling molecular‐level catalyst regulation with process‐level product management for MEK and hydrogen co‐production.

title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS
                    1
                    /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO
                    2
                    ‐to‐*NO
                    2
                    H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH
                    2
                    O‐to‐*NH
                    2
                    OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS
                    1
                    /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO
                    3
                    −
                    battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: Coking–Crosslinking Competition Shapes Alveolar Hard Carbon Formation From Heterogeneous Precursors for Wide‐Temperature Sodium Storage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Competing with lithium‐ion technology on cost and resource abundance requires sodium‐ion batteries to use hard‐carbon anodes produced from abundant, inexpensive feedstocks without sacrificing structural control. Yet the natural and residual feedstocks that meet these requirements are typically chemically heterogeneous. Competing transformations among their constituent fractions before high‐temperature treatment make the carbonization pathway and carbon architecture difficult to predict and direct. Here, controlled fraction removal and reintroduction reveal a new mechanism whereby coking‐crosslinking competition selects the carbonization pathway. Surface coking blocks oxygen access and suppresses bulk crosslinking, whereas low‐temperature pre‐purification removes coking‐prone fractions, preserving an oxygen‐accessible skeleton that forms alveolar hard carbon (AHC).
                    Operando
                    x‐ray diffraction (XRD)/Raman and synchrotron x‐ray absorption near‐edge structure (XANES) establish that the low‐potential plateau arises from reversible formation of highly reduced sodium species within confined pores. AHC‐120@15‐1400 delivers 388.3 mAh g
                    −1
                    with 91.3% initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), retains 94.3% capacity after 10 500 cycles at 4 A g
                    −1
                    , and operates from −25°C to 45°C. A 1.2 Ah pouch cell retains 82.5% capacity after 1,000 cycles, while the route lowers cradle‐to‐gate material‐resource impact by 35.6% relative to commercial hard‐carbon production. Controlling coking‐crosslinking competition establishes a pathway‐selective design principle for converting heterogeneous carbon resources into durable, wide‐temperature sodium‐storage carbons.

title: Active Targeting Across Scales in Medical Robotics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structures such as proteins. These interventions are hindered by challenges, such as biological barriers and dynamic microenvironments, which necessitate the development of more effective diagnosis, therapy, and microsurgery strategies. Multiscale medical robots are an emerging strategy to address these challenges: advances in micro and nano engineering have enabled the development of sophisticated medical robots with size adaptability and hierarchical navigation for active targeting. Such systems can connect organ‐level access and navigation with local action at tissue, cellular, or molecular scales. Here, we discuss advances in micro/nano engineering to design and fabricate multiscale medical robots, with focus on their active targeting capabilities in precision medicine. We provide an overview of the current state of these systems, from accurate diagnosis and targeted therapy to minimally invasive microsurgery across the various scales of the human body, and explore how anatomical, biological, and imaging constraints shape their design. Finally, we discuss the practical challenges of clinical translation, including system‐level assessment within the intended clinical workflow and the need for collaboration between engineers and clinicians.

title: Armoring Bubbles With Wettability‐Adaptive and Self‐Fusible Particles for Efficient Gas Handling in Air
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Mixing small quantities of gas and storing them in air is promising for developing a miniature gas reactor. Bubble encapsulation by liquid film has been considered; however, stabilizing the liquid layer while keeping bubble coalescence ability is challenging. Here, a time‐programmed wettability‐adaptive and self ‐ fusible particle is designed to modulate the coalescence ability and stability of gas bubbles. The adaptive particles remain initially hydrophobic and adsorb on the liquid layer surface, forming a stable gas‐barrier layer. After a modulated time of 10 to 600 s, the particles switch to hydrophilic and absorb available liquid. This adaptive wettability enables capillary‐driven automated coalescence of the contacting bubbles in air. After the preprogrammed time, the diffused particles self‐fuse and provide a continuous gel layer, allowing robust shell formation with tolerance to gas escape for at least 30 days. Proof of concept shows gas/gas and gas/liquid micro‐reactions and their long‐term storage.

However, synthesizing wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs is challenging due to their intrinsic isotropic bonding. Here, we present an electrochemical passivation liquid metal printing strategy that regulates oxidation kinetics via galvanic coupling, enabling the synthesis of wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs in air. title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless

The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D
                    3

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals.
