abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Despite substantial recent advances in query mapping and cell type or cell state discovery tools, their application to single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) data remains challenging. The heterogeneous nature of peak feature spaces across samples hinders the effectiveness of existing methods, while the absence of dedicated tools for detecting perturbed cell types and states in scATAC-seq data further limits the depth of downstream analyses. To address these limitations, we present EpiPack, an integrative computational toolkit that leverages heterogeneous transfer learning and graph-based modeling strategies to advance scATAC-seq analysis. At its core, the Peak Embedding Informed Variational Inference (PEIVI) framework within EpiPack enhances mappable reference construction, query mapping, and label transfer, demonstrating that leveraging heterogeneous features in scATAC-seq data outperforms methods relying solely on conventional homogeneous features. In addition, EpiPack’s global-local out-of-reference (OOR) detection framework achieves robust and efficient detection of perturbed cell types and states, extending the utility of scATAC-seq to disease and perturbation contexts. With its modular design and transferable pre-trained references, EpiPack can be readily applied to diverse analytical tasks and is available as a Python package at https://github.com/ZhangLabGT/EpiPack.

title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

abstract: Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. Herein, we propose active salt management as a proactive system function and fabricate an intelligent dynamic evaporator (IDE) that integrates in-situ sensing, adaptive decision-making, and active regulation. The asymmetrically oxidized PPy/cotton is applied for real-time monitoring of ion concentration evolution within nanochannels via hydrovoltaic actuation. Coupled with deep learning algorithms, IDE dynamically correlates electrical outputs with salt enrichment states, enabling advanced intervention before critical accumulation. Dynamic solar tracking enables uniform interfacial evaporation and ion enrichment, elevating the stability of hydrovoltaic potential signals and the recognition precision (93.8%) of salt enrichment states. Overall, radiation-adaptive and self-cleaning IDE delivers an average daily freshwater production of 12.3 kg m−2 over 100 days. This work shifts salt management from static material design to intelligent adaptive control, providing a scalable framework for robust and sustainable water purification.

title: Spontaneous N-formylation of amines with carbon monoxide in irradiated water
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: N-formyl amines are crucial synthetic intermediates, yet their production often relies on methods requiring precious metal catalysts, suffering from activation barrier or generating stoichiometric waste. Concurrently, the astrochemical origin of formamide, a prebiotic precursor, remains debated. Herein, we report a catalyst-free, radical-driven N-formylation strategy that addresses both challenges. Using only water as the solvent and X-ray or electron beam as the energy source, we achieve efficient coupling between carbon monoxide (CO) and amines under ambient conditions. Scaling up with a high-flux electron beam delivers a formamide production rate of 0.35 ± 0.01 mmol L−1 min−1, with favorable techno-economic analysis indicating industrial potential. The reaction proceeds via the in-situ generation of key radicals (•CHO from CO and •NR1R2 from amines) generated by species (eaq−, •H, •OH) produced during water radiolysis, followed by spontaneous C–N coupling. This method exhibits superior C–N coupling reactivity for most derivatives including electron-donating and electron-withdrawing group and achieves a notable radiation-chemical yield up to 4.6 × 10−7 mol J−1. Beyond synthesis, this work may offer mechanistic insights into the related radiation-driven prebiotic pathway, demonstrating that radiolysis of simple mixtures (H2O, CO, NH3) can efficiently yield formamide, thereby bridging green chemistry and astrochemistry.

title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm−2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm−1, among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

title: Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni1/2Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO2RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO2RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO2-enriched local microenvironment. Consequently, p-Ni1/2Pc catalyst exhibits a remarkable 97.5% CO Faraday efficiency (FE) and a maximum 402.9 mA cm−2 partial current density (jCO) in strong acidic electrolytes (pH = 1), while maintaining stable operation for 85 h without salt precipitation. This work highlights the critical role of symmetry-breaking in simultaneously engineering active sites and interfacial microenvironments for robust CO2RR in acidic media.

title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Mechanochemistry is an expanding and generally green synthetic route, which is attracting more and more chemists in academia and industry. Yet, its applicability is often still limited by the lack of information on the mechanochemical processes. Therefore, to help elucidating reaction pathways in the solid state, we need to develop new real time monitoring techniques. Here we present an operando study of mechanochemical syntheses relying on Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy (NQR). Two mechanochemical syntheses were followed in operando (i.e., real-time in situ) mode by NQR, namely the formation of a halogen-bonded cocrystal and the preparation of a hybrid perovskite, demonstrating potential applications of this original technique, as well as its complementarity to more conventional operando methods used in ball-milling (BM). Lastly, we show that our NQR set-up can also be used in real-time to follow the temperature evolution, during a reaction, directly inside the milling jar. This method, BM-NQR, represents a promising functional alternative to NMR spectroscopy for the real-time monitoring of ball-milling syntheses.

title: Metal-oxo clusters stabilize electron-selective interfaces for efficient perovskite solar cells
source: Joule
abstract: Efficient perovskite photovoltaics require durable interfaces compatible with scalable manufacturing. Solution-processable metal-oxo clusters combine robust inorganic frameworks with tunable organic components to enhance charge extraction and suppress ion migration. Complementary clusters stabilize both interfaces of the electron-transport layer, enabling a certified efficiency of 26.7% and improved operational stability. This modular strategy links molecular interface engineering with scalable coating, offering a pathway toward efficient, durable perovskite solar technologies.

title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest‐induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host‐guest interaction‐based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD‐inactive monoterpenoid, (–)‐carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD‐inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host‐guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δ
                    ε
                    | >80 M
                    −1
                    cm
                    −1
                    at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest‐induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M
                    −1
                    cm
                    −1
                    ). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of
                    d/l
                    ‐mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di‐ and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M
                    −1
                    cm
                    −1
                    ) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

title: Promoting CO2 Electromethanation via Reverse H‐Spillover on Zeolite Y‐Confined CuO Nanoclusters
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO
                    2
                    RR) presents a promising route for converting CO
                    2
                    emissions into valuable products, with methane (CH
                    4
                    ) being particularly attractive owing to its high energy density and infrastructure compatibility. However, selective CH
                    4
                    formation via sequential *CO hydrogenation remains kinetically challenged by competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we encapsulate CuO nanoclusters within zeolite Y, where spatial confinement enables the uniform dispersion of CuO and enhances the reverse H‐spillover (RHS)‐mediated utilization of *H species generated on the zeolite support for sequential *CO hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH
                    4
                    Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% ± 1.3% at 600 mA cm
                    −2
                    and 65.6% ± 1.0% at 1000 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Experimental and theoretical studies show that H
                    2
                    O is preferentially activated on the zeolite support, generating *H species that are rapidly transferred to adjacent CuO via RHS for CO
                    2
                    hydrogenation.
                    Operando
                    spectroscopic detection of CH
                    4
                    ‐related *OCH
                    3
                    /*CH
                    
                      x
                    
                    intermediates, together with DFT calculations, indicates that zeolite–CuO interactions favor *CO hydrogenation to *CHO over *CO dimerization, thereby promoting CH
                    4
                    formation. This work establishes spatial confinement‐coupled RHS as an effective strategy for regulating interfacial *H transfer and sequential hydrogenation in the eCO
                    2
                    RR process.

title: Precise Control of Spin–Orbit Coupling for High‐Efficiency Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence: Toward Photo‐Responsive Patterning and Visual Oxygen Sensing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photo‐responsive pure organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials rely on the compatible synergy between high phosphorescence quantum yield (
                    Φ
                    P
                    ) and high oxygen sensitivity. However, a fundamental dilemma exists: high
                    Φ
                    P
                    typically requires a shorter triplet exciton lifetime to suppress non‐radiative deactivation, whereas high oxygen sensitivity demands a longer triplet lifetime for efficient energy transfer. To resolve this contradiction, a series of pure organic RTP molecules are designed via the functional unit combination strategy. In these molecules, the flexible (4‐(tert‐butyl)phenyl)thio unit undergoes excited‐state geometric torsion, and the nonbonding n‐orbital of the sulfur atom is decoupled to varying degrees from the π‐orbital of the RTP core, enabling precise control of the spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) strength. Among them, the optimal molecule 56M2T achieves both a high oxygen sensitivity and a high
                    Φ
                    P
                    of 87.6%, exhibiting excellent photo‐responsive RTP enhancement. Based on this photo‐responsive dynamic RTP, we have further developed a high‐contrast, cyclically‐stable “optical writing & humidity erasing” photo‐responsive patterning system and a low‐cost time‐dependent method for visual oxygen sensing. This work not only provides novel insights into the molecular design of highly efficient and oxygen‐sensitive RTP materials, but also sheds light on their application in the field of intelligent responses.

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural
                    
                      m
                      CB‐Co
                    
                    and
                    
                      m
                      CB‐Ni
                    
                    MOFs, we generate two MTV MOFs with different one‐dimensional Ni/Co arrangements, resulting in distinct semiconducting and magnetic properties. High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m
                    −
                    2
                    . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: One Acceptor Core, Two Bright Pathways: CF3‐Substituted Triazines Achieve Highly Efficient Intermolecular Exciplexes and Intramolecular TADF
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT)‐based exciplexes provide broad design flexibility through independent donor and acceptor selection, but often suffer from low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) due to limited orbital overlap. In contrast, intramolecular CT‐based thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) systems can achieve high PLQYs through controlled donor‐acceptor interactions, but generally require precise molecular design and substituent tuning. Here, we show that a CF
                    3
                    ‐substituted triazine scaffold (
                    T4
                    ) serves as a unified molecular platform for achieving highly efficient emission through both intermolecular and intramolecular CT pathways. The CzCF
                    3
                    ‐substituted derivatives
                    
                      T4‐2CzCF
                      3
                    
                    and
                    
                      T4‐3CzCF
                      3
                    
                    formed highly emissive intermolecular exciplexes with mCBP, achieving PLQYs of 100%. Incorporation of stronger carbazole donors afforded
                    T4‐3Cz
                    , which exhibited intramolecular CT‐based TADF with PLQYs reaching 100% in solution and 100% in an mCBP‐doped film.
                    T4‐3Cz
                    also displayed near‐infrared multiphoton absorption, with a two‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ
                    2
                    ) of 80 GM at 780 nm and a three‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ
                    3
                    ) of 2.94 × 10
                    −80
                     cm
                    6
                    s
                    2
                    at 1210 nm. Furthermore, OLEDs based on the
                    
                      T4‐3CzCF
                      3
                    
                    intermolecular exciplex and the intramolecular CT‐based TADF emitter
                    T4‐3Cz

                    T4

title: Resilient j = 3/2 superconductivity in topological semimetal YPtBi
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cooper pairing in most of the known fermionic superfluids occurs via spin-1/2 quasiparticle interactions that lead to spin-singlet or spin-triplet pairing. In the topological semimetal YPtBi, strong spin–orbit coupling results in a band inversion between highly symmetric
                    s
                    - and
                    p
                    -like electronic bands and a degeneracy at the Γ point that ensures the manifold of
                    j
                    = 3/2 quasiparticle states thrive near the Fermi level, where superconducting pairing occurs. Here we study the effects of magnetic and nonmagnetic disorder and carrier density on this exotic superconducting pairing state. By varying levels of disorder and carrier densities by nearly two and three orders of magnitude, respectively, we show that the superconducting critical temperature of YPtBi has a remarkable robustness, with little variation across this span. Our results suggest that superconductivity in YPtBi may reside in a regime where phase stiffness, rather than pair formation, governs the transition temperature. The insensitivity of Cooper pairing to dramatic changes in quasiparticle environment in a
                    j
                    = 3/2 superconductor highlights a form of protection realized in topological high-spin superconductors.

title: Anomeric configuration encodes mesophase preference of glucosylceramides in phospholipid membranes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Glycosphingolipids are key components of the cell glycocalyx, yet the extent to which their anomeric configuration affects their membrane organization remains unclear. Glucosylceramide (GlcCer) exists as α- and β-anomers with distinct biological activities, while the biophysical basis for these differences is unknown. Here, using nitroxide spin-labeled analogs of α- and β-GlcCer, we examined how the glycosidic stereochemistry affects their partitioning in phospholipid bilayers. In 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine, dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine, and distearoylphosphatidylcholine liposomes, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra of both probes contained two components: a broad, motion-restricted component consistent with GlcCer incorporated into the lamellar lipid bilayer and a sharp, highly mobile component attributed to some segregated, bilayer-associated GlcCer-rich nano-assemblies. EPR spectral simulations and complementary analyses showed that α-GlcCer predominantly partitioned into the lamellar phospholipid phase, whereas β-GlcCer was strongly enriched in the segregated GlcCer-rich phase. Importantly, analogous anomer-dependent EPR behavior was also observed for aqueous GlcCer dispersions in the absence of phospholipids, indicating that the distinct assembly propensities are intrinsic to the glycolipids and are modulated, rather than created, by the phospholipids. These findings support a two-mesophase model in which anomeric configuration acts as a stereochemical switch that biases GlcCer between phospholipid lamellae and segregated glycolipid nano-assemblies. Notably, such anomer-dependent behaviors were observed at a probe loading of only 0.5 mol%. Thus, even at rather low abundance, a subtle stereochemical difference in GlcCer can substantially alter its compatibility with a phospholipid membrane matrix, providing a plausible physical basis for anomer-dependent glycolipid sorting, signaling, and disease-associated membrane organization.

title: Unconventional modulation of Nav1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Voltage-gated sodium (Na
                    v
                    ) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Na
                    v
                    channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from
                    Lychas mucronatus
                    . LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Na
                    v
                    1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNa
                    v
                    1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSD
                    II
                    ) and the extracellular loop III (ECL
                    III
                    ) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3–S4
                    II
                    loop and displaces S0/S3
                    II
                    helices to trap VSD
                    II
                    within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSD
                    II
                    conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSD
                    II
                    trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECL
                    III
                    engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECL
                    III
                    region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Na
                    v
                    channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Na
                    v
                    channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

title: Intrinsically disordered ligands for the control of receptor uptake by endocytosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Endocytosis plays a crucial role in signaling, recycling, and degradation of receptors. Controlling endocytosis of specific receptors is therefore a major goal for both basic science and medicine. While antibody-induced dimerization can drive signaling-induced uptake of some receptors, the steric bulk of antibodies generally inhibits endocytosis, such that control over receptor uptake remains an unmet need. Recent work has demonstrated that attractive interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins drive inward membrane curvature, a key step in endocytosis. To harness this phenomenon for the control of receptor uptake, we designed chimeras that consisted of disordered domains fused to ligands for specific receptors. These chimeras condensed on membrane surfaces, in agreement with computational modeling, driving receptor clustering and uptake via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. In contrast, chimeras that repelled one another resisted condensation, helping receptors escape endocytosis and remain on the cell surface. Taken together, these results suggest that by modulating the amino acid sequence of intrinsically disordered ligands, we can promote or hinder the internalization of specific receptors by endocytic pathways. More broadly, these findings suggest a generalizable strategy for controlling the plasma membrane lifetime of diverse receptors, opening up new pathways for modulating cellular behavior and delivering therapeutics.

title: Acetate–FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are required for the protective effects of acetate, which are also dependent on FFAR2 signaling and IL-22. Neutrophil-specific deletion of FFAR2 impairs IL-22 responses, increases epithelial damage, and exacerbates colitis, while administration of recombinant IL-22 is sufficient to restore acetate protection in this context. Analysis of human ulcerative colitis biopsies reveals increased FFAR2
                    +
                    neutrophils correlating with IL-22-related gene signatures. These findings indicate that acetate–FFAR2–neutrophil–IL-22 axis modulates intestinal inflammation, revealing a metabolic mechanism that links microbiota-derived signals to mucosal protection and highlighting potential therapeutic targets for inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these “vaccinal” effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell–dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our findings identify the Fc–FcγR axis as a critical determinant of the reliable induction of durable remission and provide a mechanistic framework for developing Fc-engineered bNAbs designed to enhance vaccinal immunity and advance antibody-based strategies with the potential to achieve functional cure.

title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client–scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client–scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client–scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue–resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.

title: SCN1B intron 3 retention results in a nonsense-mediated decay–sensitive mRNA linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Biallelic variants in the voltage-gated sodium channel (VGSC) gene
                    SCN1B
                    are linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy type 52 (DEE52).
                    SCN1B
                    encodes two isoforms: transmembrane β1, generated by all 6 coding exons, and β1B, generated by exons 1 to 3 followed by retention of intron 3 (
                    SCN1B
                    -IR). Transmembrane β1 subunits are multifunctional proteins that regulate sodium current and channel cell-surface expression, participate in cell–cell and cell–matrix adhesion, and modulate transcription. Several DEE52 variants in the transmembrane β1 coding region have been shown to result in mixed loss-of-function. DEE52 variants are also identified in
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, yet their functional impacts remain unknown. Here, we provide evidence that
                    SCN1B
                    -IR is a cell type–specific, nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)–sensitive transcript. We investigate a severe biallelic DEE52 patient variant in intron 3,
                    SCN1B
                    c.449-2A>G, which results in expression of
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, but not transmembrane β1 transcripts. A transgenic mouse model that expresses
                    SCN1B
                    -IR, but not transmembrane β1, transcript phenocopies
                    Scn1b
                    null mice with seizures and early death. Thus,
                    SCN1B
                    -IR functions as an NMD-sensitive transcript that cannot compensate for the loss of transmembrane β1. We propose that future work may reveal
                    SCN1B
                    -IR to be a therapeutic target similar to other NMD-targeted transcripts.

title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype–phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype–phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar “frequency matching” results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the “replicated genotype–phenotype map” for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

title: Intranasal delivery of a ROS-activatable myeloperoxidase inhibitor alleviates Alzheimer’s-like symptoms and pathology
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are important contributors to Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Myeloperoxidase (MPO), a key driver of oxidative inflammation released mainly by activated microglia in the neurodegenerative brain, is a potential therapeutic target to inhibit the neuroinflammatory cascade and oxidative damage in AD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unexplored, and achieving targeted brain delivery of an MPO inhibitor and minimizing systemic effects remain significant challenges. We addressed these limitations by first establishing that genetic deletion of MPO in the 5XFAD mouse model improved memory performance and reduced amyloid deposition, validating MPO as a therapeutic target. We then developed a liposome-encapsulated reactive oxygen species (ROS)-activatable MPO inhibitor (LERAMI). LERAMI uniquely combines targeted delivery with on-demand drug release, utilizing a ROS-sensitive linker to selectively release MPO inhibitors in ROS-rich regions within the AD microenvironment, minimizing off-target effects and systemic toxicity. In the 5XFAD mouse model. By reducing MPO expression and activity, LERAMI significantly improved cognitive performance, accompanied by decreased microglial activation, attenuated oxidative DNA damage, improved synaptic and neuronal density, and reduced amyloid burden. RNA sequencing revealed a robust hippocampal transcriptomic reprogramming, with upregulation of pathways critical for synaptic plasticity, calcium signaling, axon guidance, and neuroprotection, along with downregulation of inflammatory and immune response pathways. These findings demonstrate that targeted ROS-activatable MPO inhibition with LERAMI represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD and potentially other neuroinflammatory diseases, offering a unique approach to mitigate neuroinflammation, preserve synaptic integrity, and restore cognitive function.

title: In This Issue
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Fossilized red blood cells in dinosaur bonePreserved organic tissues and molecules have previously been reported in fossils.However, the identification of preserved tissues and molecules is controversial, given rapid degradation and the possibility of contamination.Kliti Grice et al. report the identification of fossilized red blood cells (RBCs) within the vascular canals of hind limb bones from Aratasaurus museunacionali, a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur from Brazil.The vascular canals contain abundant spherical microstructures with a morphology resembling RBCs.A combination of imaging, spectroscopic, and molecular analyses identified a consistent association of the RBC-like microstructures with manganese oxide.Analysis of bone extracts identified heme B-a key molecule in blood-and products of heme B reduction.The mineralized microstructures were localized to the vascular canals.The microstructures' molecular signatures contrasted with those of the microbial mat surrounding the fossil, supporting the origin of the heme biomarkers within the bone rather than through contamination.The authors suggest that manganese mineral stabilization of the RBCs facilitated the preservation of the heme longer than previously thought possible.According to the authors, analysis of blood-derived biomolecules in fossils could provide insights into the physiology, oxygen transport, and evolutionary biology of ancient life.-M.H. Illustration of heme and heme breakdown products in individual RBCs preserved in limb bone material of the theropod dinosaur Aratasaurus.

title: A circuit mechanism for psychosis vulnerability during perimenopause
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The transition to menopause is a period of profound physiological change that encompasses nearly one-third of a woman’s lifespan and is associated with a distinct rise in the incidence of psychosis. Despite the clinical burden of menopause-associated psychosis, the circuit-level mechanisms linking reproductive aging to psychiatric vulnerability remain poorly defined. Current understanding is limited by rodent models that utilize abrupt surgical hormone loss, which fail to capture the progressive endocrine fluctuations and follicular depletion characteristic of the natural menopausal transition. Here, we investigate how the gradual transition from perimenopause to postmenopause regulates the ventral hippocampus-mesolimbic dopamine circuit, a pathway centrally implicated in the development of psychotic symptoms. Specifically, we show that the perimenopausal transition induces a transient state of ventral hippocampal hyperactivity that selectively drives dopamine system dysfunction, whereas this modulatory control is absent in the postmenopausal state. These findings reveal that psychosis-related circuit instability is precipitated specifically by the hormonal transition itself, rather than the persistent state of estrogen deficiency that follows. This contrasts with the long-standing “estrogen protection hypothesis,” which posits that low hormone levels are the primary driver of symptoms and explains why standard hormone replacement and antipsychotic therapies often yield inconsistent results. Our results establish that perimenopause is a mechanistically distinct neurobiological window characterized by a unique failure of hippocampal-dopamine circuit regulation. By identifying this specific period of circuit instability, this work provides a framework for stage-specific psychiatric interventions and reframes reproductive aging as a series of distinct transitions in brain function.

title: Neurovascular protein half-lives in health and aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Specializations of blood vasculature in the central nervous system (CNS), including the blood–brain barrier (BBB), neurovascular coupling, and perivascular spaces, maintain CNS homeostasis and become dysfunctional in disease and aging. Protein turnover, the process by which proteins are continually degraded and replaced, profoundly influences cell and tissue function and is dysregulated in aging and disease. Understanding the turnover of neurovascular proteins could provide insight into how the vasculature achieves both long-term structural stability and dynamic regulation. Vascular proteins, however, are underrepresented in previous studies of in vivo brain protein turnover. In this work, we used stable isotope labeling, nonenzymatic blood vessel enrichment, and high-resolution mass spectrometry-based proteomics to quantify the half-lives of brain vascular proteins in young adult and aged mice. We report half-life estimates for 1,358 proteins, including components of endothelial junctions, BBB transporters, astrocyte endfoot proteins, and vascular basement membrane proteins. We found that certain classes of proteins with related functions had similar half-lives, including BBB junctional proteins (~3 d), BBB transporters (~2 to 6 d), and most basement membrane components (>30 d). We also identified peptide motifs enriched in proteins with short and long half-lives and found differences in half-life distributions for cell type–specific proteomes. Finally, although we did not observe a global age-related shift in vascular protein turnover, we did identify specific proteins with increased or decreased half-lives in aging. This work establishes a high-quality database of neurovascular protein half-lives and provides a foundation for understanding how protein turnover contributes to neurovascular function and age-associated dysfunction.

title: Visualization of actin filaments in Plasmodium falciparum blood cell stages
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The actin cytoskeleton is crucial to regulate cellular processes and morphology in eukaryotes, yet the tools to visualize it are not compatible with all organisms. In the apicomplexan
                    Plasmodium falciparum
                    , actin filaments are thought to be short and unstable, complicating their visualization. Here, we show that a tandem fusion of the actin-chromobody can label filaments in all
                    P. falciparum
                    red blood cell stages and observe actin structures in live cells with high spatiotemporal resolution. This work suggests that previous lack of labeling was due to suboptimal probes and that malaria blood stages have a filamentous and highly dynamic actin network.

title: Single-molecule FRET at 30: Toward conformational sequencing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Single-molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer (smFRET) turned 30 this year. We argue that three advances usually treated as separate endeavors, i.e., high-information-content per-molecule readout, sequence-linked massive parallelism, and automated trajectory decoding, are in fact one convergence that is turning smFRET from a one-molecule-at-a-time measurement into a high-throughput conformational sequencer, a platform that measures dynamic conformational phenotypes across sequence space at scale. This perspective traces the 30-y arc, forecasts which advances will prove most transformative over the next decade, states the conditions on which that forecast depends, and identifies the bottlenecks that still remain.

title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

title: Diffusive and advective transport in structurally anisotropic fibrous hydrogels
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Changes in fiber orientation in structurally anisotropic fibrous extracellular matrices govern transport, distribution, and accumulation of biologically active molecules and therapeutic nanoparticles in tissues. Fundamental studies of advection-driven transport in such matrices are challenging because changes in network anisotropy are generally coupled with variation in fiber dimensions, density, and surface chemistry. Here, a fibrous hydrogel was engineered in which the type and degree of fiber orientation were decoupled from these structural characteristics. Advection of charge-neutral nanoparticle probes under physiologically relevant pressure gradients was studied in a channel geometry that imposed spatially nonuniform flow across the fibrous network. The probe advection was quantified by the time of probe permeation through the gel along the fastest flow path and the time of probe distribution within the gel. We show that the permeation timescale was governed by advection along the pressure gradient, whereas the distribution timescale transitioned between advection- and diffusion-limited behavior depending on fiber orientation and probe dimension. The decoupling between these timescales became more pronounced with stronger alignment along the pressure gradient and with increasing probe dimension. Scaling analysis and a fluid dynamics simulation model further provided mechanistic insight into these experimental findings. Together, these results identify the key structural factors governing advection in anisotropic fibrous networks and provide a platform for future studies of the role of fiber orientation in tissues in regulating the transport, distribution, and dissemination of biologically active molecules, exosomes, and nanoparticle therapeutics under interstitial fluid flow.

title: Multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived biomimetic vesicles for cancer multimodal targeting and immune reprogramming
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Despite advances of biomimetic vesicles in cancer therapy, clinical challenges such as biosafety, scalability, and therapeutic efficacy remain significant hurdles. To address these limitations, we reveal the critical tumor-homing motifs of cancer cell membrane vesicles: a synergistic “chemotactic recruitment-adhesion anchoring” cascade effect, especially chemokine axes (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4) and integrins (e.g., αVβ3). In this study, we identify autologous fibroblasts as an ideal “chassis” cell for engineering biomimetic carriers. Using this platform, we construct multigene-engineered fibroblast-derived nanovesicles (X-Fb-MNVs) coexpressing critical chemokine receptor CXCR4 and adhesion ligand iRGD, as well as PD-1 and CD47 protein, which achieved robust and broad-spectrum tumor targeting across breast, liver, pancreatic, and colon cancer PDX models. Significantly, CD47-modified X-Fb-MNVs reduced hepatic accumulation and phagocytic clearance, thereby minimizing off-target effects in vivo and improving tumor targeting efficiency. By loading diABZI STING agonist into X-Fb-MNVs with overexpressed PD-1, our system activates both T cell and innate immunity, reversing ICB resistance and achieving 83.3% survival with no tumor recurrence and long-term immune surveillance over 90 d, whereas no mice survived with free diABZI treatment. By merging multimodal targeting, immune reprogramming, and scalable production into a single platform, X-Fb-MNVs represent a remarkable biomimetic system with transformative potential for a wide-spectrum cancer immunotherapy.

title: Competitive disruption of COI1 receptor assembly by a hemibiotrophic bacterial effector suppresses jasmonate-mediated immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Hormone pathways are central hubs in plant immunity, and their receptors, the critical initiators of signaling cascades, are logical targets of pathogen effectors. The jasmonic acid (JA) pathway is a cornerstone of defense against phytopathogens, especially necrotrophs. However, whether pathogens can directly target its receptor COI1 to subvert this defense layer has remained unclear. Here, we show that JA signaling positively regulates resistance to the devastating hemibiotrophic pathogen
                    Ralstonia solanacearum
                    and identified a bacterial effector, RipBO, that directly targets COI1 to counteract this defense. RipBO binds with high affinity to the F-box domain of COI1, competitively disrupts the COI1-ASK interaction, and thereby blocks SCF
                    COI1
                    complex assembly. This disruption effectively stabilizes JAZ repressors and paralyzes JA-mediated immunity. Our findings clarify the contribution of JA signaling to bacterial wilt resistance and identify direct targeting of the hormone receptor as a pathogen virulence strategy, pointing to a potential vulnerability for crop protection.

title: Structural insights into inhibition and activation mechanisms of plant calcium-dependent protein kinases
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) comprise the major group of Ca
                    2+
                    -regulated kinases in plants and protists. These enzymes comprise an N-terminal kinase domain and a C-terminal Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent activation domain (CAD). We solved the crystal structures of autoinhibited and activated forms of a plant CDPK,
                    Arabidopsis
                    CPK3. In the autoinhibited form, the CAD resembles a “dumbbell-like” calmodulin protein with a long helix in the N terminus that inhibits the kinase domain in a pseudo-substrate manner. Upon Ca
                    2+
                    binding to the four EF-hands, CAD undergoes a dramatic conformational change with a rotation around the kinase domain, thus exposing its active site for substrate recognition. Our structural and biochemical studies reveal that most plant CDPKs may involve distinct mechanisms of activation compared with CDPKs from the apicomplexan parasites.

title: Activation of ROPGEFs by a malectin-like receptor kinase is involved in tip growth regulation in Physcomitrium patens
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Rho-type GTPases of plants (ROPs) play essential roles in polarized cell growth, cell division, and organogenesis. Their activation depends on two types of guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs): the plant-specific PRONE-domain-containing ROPGEFs and DOCK-type SPKGEFs. While ROPGEFs have been proposed to be autoinhibited in pollen and activated by receptor-like kinases (RLKs), the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Using the moss
                    Physcomitrium patens
                    , we show that moss ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 exhibit low intrinsic GEF activity and are not autoinhibited by non-PRONE regions, whereas the catalytic domain of SPK1 and SPK6 is highly active. Through a candidate screen, we identified MLRK1, a malectin-like receptor kinase, as a ROPGEF-interacting protein. MLRK1 directly phosphorylates ROPGEF4 and ROPGEF6 and stimulates their GEF activities in vitro. These effects are attenuated by substituting key phosphosites (Ser231 in ROPGEF4 and Ser524/Thr526 in ROPGEF6) with nonphosphorylatable residues. Structural modeling, pull-down assays, and functional analyses indicate that phosphorylation enhances ROPGEF-ROP interactions and promotes the membrane localization of ROPGEF4/6. Furthermore, ROPGEFs are not essential for polarized cell growth on their own but act redundantly with SPK2. At the apical membrane, ROPGEFs appear to activate ROPs, reduce their diffusion, promote actin filament assembly and vesicle secretion, and ultimately facilitate cell expansion and growth. Collectively, our findings provide functional evidence that RLK-ROPGEF-ROP signaling module has emerged in early land plants and is involved in cell growth regulation.

title: Domain-encoded DNA barcodes for combinatorial multiplexed protein imaging via stepwise displacement
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Multiplexed protein imaging via DNA barcoding faces a fundamental scaling constraint: Each target requires a distinct DNA identity, making barcode capacity grow only linearly with the number of validated sequences. Combinatorial encoding in RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization achieves exponential scaling by distributing shared readout sequences across dozens of probes per transcript, but antibody-based protein labeling lacks this multiprobe architecture. Here, we report domain-encoded DNA barcodes (DEDBs), which embed combinatorial identity within the internal domain organization of a single-stranded DNA scaffold. Three orthogonal encoding units arranged across three encoding domains define a theoretical design space of 27 barcodes. Sequence reuse does not compromise readout specificity: Each read strand spans two adjacent domains, so a mismatched read strand inevitably contains a continuous stretch of noncomplementary bases and forms a thermodynamically disfavored intermediate that is subsequently displaced by the perfectly matched strand. We term this self-correcting behavior thermodynamic proofreading, and a three-process kinetic model shows that specificity arises not from initial binding discrimination but from cognate-driven correction at the product level. Coupled with signal-amplified antibody labeling, DEDBs enable quantitatively decoded nine-target intracellular protein imaging in fixed cells. The same barcode library supports Polychrome trajectory decoding for combinatorial identification and Monochrome cycle-resolved visualization for direct single-target inspection through reconfiguration of read-strand labeling. By generating combinatorial identities through the positional arrangement of reusable sequences within a single DNA strand, DEDBs reframe DNA barcode design from sequence enumeration to positional encoding.

title: Endosomal mRNA transport coordinates local mitochondrial bioenergetics during polar fungal growth
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mitochondrial function relies on the precise spatial coordination of protein synthesis and import. Most mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and must be supplied across varying intracellular distances. In highly polarized cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, active long-distance mRNA transport is thought to sustain distal mitochondrial function, but its mechanistic coupling to protein import and organelle physiology is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that endosomal transport of mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins orchestrates local bioenergetics in infectious hyphae of
                    Ustilago maydis
                    . Using the subunit Atp3 of electron transport chain Complex V as a model, we uncover that the endosomal mRNA transporter Rrm4 is required for efficient mitochondrial protein import, particularly at growth poles. Loss of Rrm4 leads to defects in mitochondrial import, resulting in altered physiology. We propose that endosome-coupled mRNA transport constitutes a fundamental layer of subcellular mitochondrial homeostasis, with implications extending from fungal pathogenicity to neuronal disease.

title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women’s behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers’ gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more persuaded than men. To the extent that men and women emphasize different topics in political conversations and have different discussion partners, these dynamics are likely to shape women’s political persuasive influence.

title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:

title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C19, C24, and C29 Terpenoids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Downstream conversion with 20 diterpene synthases (DTSs) and 10 sesterterpene synthases (StTSs) yielded in total 24 new compounds. Surprisingly, in two cases the substrate analogs were converted by GGPPS and a DTS into

title: Photocatalytic Biomass Valorization: Electronic Polarization Enables Oxygen Activation and Selective C─C Bond Cleavage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic valorization of biomass into value‐added chemicals requires catalysts capable of simultaneously activating molecular oxygen and controlling C─C bond cleavage. In this work, we introduce an electronic polarization engineering strategy by integrating CF

                    2
                    −
                    ). Density functional theory calculations reveals that this electronic modulation lowers the energetic barrier for the key C─C bond cleavage step. Therefore, this work establishes a general framework for coupling electronic polarization with active‐site engineering to help perform selective oxidation chemistry in solar‐driven catalysis.

title: Tailoring Alkyl Chain Length to Customize Dual‐Electrode Interface for Reversible Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry in Zn–I2 Pouch Batteries (Adv. Mater. 64/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries Tetraethylammonium bromide (TEAB) customizes the microenvironment of the dual-electrode interface by zinc interface regulation and high valence iodine anchoring, activating the reversible four-electron iodine chemistry in Zn–I2 pouch batteries. More details can be found in the Research Article by Huibing He and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.75298).

title: Synergistic Bimolecular Reconstruction of the Perovskite‐Carbon Interface Enables 23.6%‐Efficiency Fully Printable Mesoscopic Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Hole‐conductor‐free, fully printable mesoscopic perovskite solar cells (p‐MPSCs) hold compelling promise for photovoltaic industrialization. However, their power conversion efficiency (PCE) remains constrained by limited hole collection at the perovskite‐carbon interface. Here, we introduce a synergistic bimolecular post‐treatment using toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and 4‐methyl sulfonyl phenyl methylammonium chloride (MSBH) to reconstruct this critical interface. We demonstrate that TDI reacts with surface formamidinium to polish and activate the perovskite terminations, while MSBH subsequently grafts onto this activated surface. This combined action simultaneously reconstructs the interface with optimized surface energy band bending and minimized interfacial defects, thereby facilitating hole extraction and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, this strategy elevates the PCE of small‐area p‐MPSCs (0.1 cm
                    2
                    ) to 23.6%. Furthermore, it enables the fabrication of a p‐MPSC minimodule with an active area of 52.7 cm
                    2
                    , achieving a PCE of 22.1%, among the highest values ever reported for carbon‐based, fully printable architectures. Devices retained 98% of their initial PCE after 750 h of operational stability testing at 55°C ± 5°C. This work provides an effective interface reconstruction strategy that concurrently addresses defect passivation and energy alignment, paving the way for high‐performance, stable, and scalable cost‐effective perovskite photovoltaics.
